title: secondary: the transfer (from) property is mandatory

detection.reason: what a secondary block LACKS cannot be told from the projection — its option keys are collected (agent 0.4.58+) but absence of one is not a match

remediation: Every `secondary` block must name where to transfer the zone from; a block without it fails Corefile parsing from 1.12.2.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*secondary\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed secondary block must carry a transfer from line

title: bind: no reverse zone for link-local IPv4 any more

detection.reason: which addresses a bind directive resolves to is host state

quote: plugin/bind: Remove zone for link-local IPv4
remediation: Reverse lookups for 169.254.0.0/16 addresses are no longer answered by the bound server; nothing to do unless something resolved link-local PTRs through CoreDNS.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*bind\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed bind directive stops serving the link-local reverse zone

title: DNS-over-QUIC: concurrent streams are capped

detection.reason: server-block zone lines (quic://…) are not collected

quote: plugin/quic: Limit concurrent DoQ streams and goroutines
remediation: Heavy DoQ clients that opened unbounded streams are throttled from 1.12.2; watch for client-side timeouts after the hop.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*quic://")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed DoQ server block enforces a stream cap

title: file/auto: REFUSED when no next plugin is available

detection.reason: plugin order is fixed by CoreDNS; whether a block has a plugin after file/auto is a Corefile fact reduced to directive names

quote: plugin/file: Return REFUSED when no next plugin is available
remediation: Names outside a file/auto zone in a block with nothing after them get REFUSED instead of SERVFAIL from 1.12.3; add `fallthrough` plus a forward if the block was meant to recurse.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*(file|auto)\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed file/auto block answers REFUSED for names it does not own
coversNotes: plugin/auto: Return REFUSED when no next plugin is available

title: route53: ported to AWS SDK v2 — credential and endpoint resolution change

detection.reason: how the route53 plugin authenticates (env, shared config, IRSA) is pod environment, which is not collected

quote: plugin/route53: Port to AWS Go SDK v2
remediation: SDK v2 resolves credentials, regions and endpoints differently (no `AWS_SDK_LOAD_CONFIG` gate, IMDSv2 by default, endpoint options). Test the route53 plugin's auth path on 1.12.3 before rolling it out.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*route53\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed route53 block authenticates through SDK v2 after 1.12.3

title: header: an action line without the query|response selector is rejected

detection.reason: read from the option KEY names the agent extracts inside each Corefile plugin block of every kube-system ConfigMap whose name contains coredns (agent 0.4.58+; older agents leave this NOT_DETECTABLE) — keys only, never values; import lines are not followed — a header option line whose first token is the action (set/clear) omits the selector; the compliant form starts with query or response

remediation: Prefix every action inside `header { … }` with `query` or `response` (`header { response set ra }`), the selector form introduced in 1.9.4. A line like `set ra` used to default to response; from 1.12.4 it fails Corefile parsing (`invalid selector`) and CoreDNS does not start.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*(set|clear)\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # a printed set/clear line inside a header block has no selector and is rejected at 1.12.4

title: prometheus: the metrics HTTP server now has timeouts

detection.reason: scrape latency is observed at the scraper, not in cluster objects

quote: plugin/metrics: Add timeouts to metrics HTTP server
remediation: Very slow scrapers (or huge /metrics pages) can be cut off by the new server timeouts from 1.12.4; check for scrape errors after the hop.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*prometheus\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed metrics endpoint enforces request timeouts

title: trace: Datadog exporter moved to dd-trace-go v2

detection.reason: the tracing backend is outside the cluster inventory

quote: plugin/trace: Migrate dd-trace-go v1 to v2
remediation: Datadog-backed trace setups should re-verify agent compatibility and tag names after 1.12.4.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n kube-system get cm -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("coredns")) | .metadata.name as $n | (.data // {})[] | split("\n")[] | select(test("^\\s*trace\\b")) | $n + ": " + .'  # each printed trace directive pointing at Datadog uses the v2 client
